1-1: Let's compare and see which one is bigger.
reading of 並べる (to line up)
correct reading of 比べる (to compare)
reading of 浮かべる (to float / to recall)
The kun-reading of 比 is くら(べる). 比べる = to compare. ならべて and しらべて are real words, but they use different kanji (並・調).
1-2: She is a close friend from my high school days.
correct reading of 親しい (close, intimate)
The kun-reading of 親 here is した(しい). 親しい友人 = a close friend. The other three are also い-adjectives, but with different meanings and kanji.
1-3: I want to enter a national university, not a private one.
くにたち is only a place name in Tokyo
correct reading of 国立 (national, state-run)
国 = こく (on-reading), 立 = りつ. 国立 = national. 私立 (しりつ) = private. くにたち is a city name in Tokyo and does not fit here.
1-4: I'm good at math, but weak at English.
correct reading of 苦手 (weak at, dislike)
苦手 has a special reading: 苦 = にが, 手 = て → にがて. It is the opposite of 得意 (good at).
1-5: I told her how I felt.
correct reading of 伝える (to tell, convey)
The kun-reading of 伝 is つた(える). 気持ちを伝える = to convey one's feelings.
1-6: I was told to cheer up, because failure is the foundation of success.
失 (しつ) + 敗 (はい) changes sound when joined: しっぱい (つ becomes small っ, は becomes ぱ).
1-7: correct reading of 人間 (human being)
人間 = にんげん. Here 人 is read にん and 間 is read げん. じん/かん do not apply to this word.
1-8: Please look at the fifth line of this page.
correct reading of 五行目 (fifth line)
When counting lines, 行 is read ぎょう (一行目 = いちぎょうめ). 目 = the ~th → め.
1-9: Mr. Tanaka worked very hard and got his nutritionist qualification.
どりょく = 努力. 努 = to strive. 労力 is a real word, but it is read ろうりょく.
1-10: Father went to the park taking my younger brother with him.
連れる (to take someone along) correct
つれる = 連れる. 連 = to link, accompany. 釣れる means a fish gets caught.
1-11: The person in charge is not here today, so please come tomorrow.
かかり = 係 (the person responsible). 係の者 = the staff in charge.
1-12: The exam results were announced today.
けっか = 結果. 結 = to tie / conclude, 果 = fruit. Combinations with 課 or 決 are not real words.
1-13: うたがう = 疑う. Don't mix it up with 歌う (うたう): うた-が-う has a が.
1-14: I ordered coffee at the coffee shop.
ちゅうもん = 注文. 注 = to pour / pay attention, 文 = writing. 注門 is not a word.
1-15: This watch is old, but I really like it.
After 「古いけれども」 comes the speaker's feeling: 気に入っている = I like it. 似合う = to suit a person; it doesn't fit a watch alone.
1-16: It's cold today, so you should wear a long-sleeved shirt.
寒い → you need something warm. 長そで = long sleeves. The other three are about patterns, not about cold.
1-17: I'll pay the bill at this restaurant.
With 払う (to pay), 代金 = the price of goods or service. 現金 (cash) is a way to pay, not the bill.
1-18: Let's all split the bill for today's party.
みんなで～にしよう = let's all do ~. 割り勘 = split the bill. おごり means one person pays, which doesn't fit みんなで.
1-19: "My beard has grown. I have to shave."
Only 「ひげ」 fits with 伸びる (to grow) and そる (to shave).
1-20: Oh, you're wearing a lovely ring.
Japanese uses different verbs for wearing: 指輪をはめる, 靴をはく, ネクタイをしめる.
1-21: If you leave the car with the key inserted, it will be stolen.
to bump into, reach the end
キーを差し込む = to insert the key. ～たままで = leaving it in that state.
1-22: My older brother was in a traffic accident and was hospitalized.
事故にあう = to have an accident (遭う). It is a fixed pair, so memorize it.
1-23: When I opened a bank account, they gave me a passbook and an ATM card.
When you open an account (口座), you get a 通帳 = passbook. It pairs with キャッシュカード.
1-24: When I cancelled the trip booking the day before, not a single yen came back.
お金が返ってこなかった = no refund after cancelling. So キャンセル.
1-25: Transfer the university tuition to the designated account.
口座に振り込む = to transfer money to an account. Paying fees to a designated account is 振り込む.
1-26: Unusually, the train was almost empty yesterday.
がらがら = almost empty (train, shop). So とても空いていた.
1-27: You need a seal to withdraw savings at the bank counter.
預金を引き出す = to withdraw money = お金をおろす. Same meaning.
1-28: An urgent job came up, so I changed the travel dates.
日程を変更 = change the schedule = 日程をずらす (shift the dates). 取り消す is cancel, not change.
1-29: 横断する = to cross = 渡る.
1-30: ひかえる = to refrain, try not to do = しないようにする.
1-31: 敷く = to spread out, lay out
putting a plate on a table needs 置いて
a sofa being placed needs 置いて あります
turning on a tap needs ひねって
laying a futon on the floor: correct
敷く = to spread something flat on a floor or surface (futon, carpet). So only 布団を敷いて寝ます is correct.
1-32: cool air needs エアコン
weight on a scale needs 重さ
high calories needs カロリー
栄養のバランス = nutritional balance. The other sentences need a different word.
1-33: washing lots of clothes needs 洗濯する
storing food in the fridge: correct
keeping a pet needs 飼う
保存 = keeping something without it spoiling. 冷蔵庫で保存 is the natural use.
1-34: dirty from age needs 汚れて
wetting a cloth needs 濡らして
I spilled juice and got my skirt dirty: correct
汚す = someone makes something dirty (transitive). 汚れる = to get dirty by itself.
1-35: selfish children are not loved by everyone: wrong meaning
don't trouble your mother by being selfish: correct
a prank at the door needs いたずら
wagging its tail at everyone needs 人なつっこい
わがままを言う = to be selfish, demand your own way. The other sentences don't fit the meaning.
1-36: The more you read this book, the more interesting it gets.
〜ば〜ほど means "the more A, the more B".
1-37: Because the train stopped, I was late for an important meeting.
〜たために shows a cause, often followed by a bad result.
1-38: I still can't believe that the dog, which was so lively, has died.
1-39: Thanks to my friend's help, the move finished quickly.
おかげで = thanks to (good result). せいで is for bad results.
1-40: When I cooked it exactly as written in the cookbook, it turned out delicious.
〜とおりに = exactly as, in the same way.
1-41: This shop is open from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
AからBまで = from A to B.
1-42: On my way to the station, I stopped at the post office to send a letter.
〜ついでに = while doing A, also do B.
1-43: In this dormitory, the rule is to be back by 10 p.m.
〜ことになっている = it is the rule / it has been decided.
1-44: A friend visited right in the middle of my meal.
〜ている最中に = right in the middle of doing something.
1-45: I wrote big letters so that people at the back could see too.
〜ように shows purpose after non-volitional verbs like 見える.
1-46: A: "I'm going to Kyoto next week." B: "If you're going to Kyoto, be sure to see Kinkakuji."
〜なら is used to give advice about what the other person said.
1-47: Lately it's been nothing but rainy days, so the laundry never dries.
〜ばかり = nothing but (often with a complaining feeling).
1-48: For your own action use humble お〜します. お〜になります is for the other person's action.
1-49: This room is a little bigger than the old one, but it is not big enough.
Order: 少し 広い ことは(★) 広いが. 「AことはAが」 = it is A, but not enough.
1-50: My little brother has just learned to ride a bike and seems to be having so much fun.
Order: 乗れる ようになった ばかりで(★) 楽しくて. 〜たばかり = just did; 〜てしかたがない = extremely.
1-51: Just because you have money doesn't mean you can be happy.
Order: あるから と いって(★) 幸せになれる. 〜からといって〜わけではない = just because… doesn't mean.
1-52: I brought an umbrella thinking it would rain, but in the end I didn't need it, so it was just extra baggage.
Order: けれど 結局 使わずに(★) 済んだので. 〜ずに済む = get by without doing.
1-53: "But however expensive it is, it won't cost 50,000 yen."
Order: いくら 高い といっても(★) 5万円は.
1-54: She never misses it, rain or snow.
1-55: Besides, my grandmother is also good at cooking.
それに adds another good point.
1-56: She worked hard at rehabilitation every day.
The subject is grandmother herself, so use the plain form.
1-57: Whenever I get tired of studying, I always think of my grandmother.
〜と、いつも〜 = every time that happens.
1-58: I want to become someone who can keep doing anything, like my grandmother.
It is the writer's own wish: 〜たいと思っています.
1-59: What must people with heavy baggage do?
The notice says people with heavy baggage should tell Yamamoto by the Friday of the previous week (the 7th).
1-60: What does the writer do now?
not said he never uses it
"When I want to look something up, I always stop first" is the answer.
1-61: What must Kim do, and by when?
Tuesday was before the old date
The presentation moved to Friday and materials must be sent "by the day before", so by Thursday. The teacher makes the copies.
1-62: "Please reply to Mr/Ms Sato by phone today." Nakamura changes the room booking.
1-63: Why was the garbage bag returned?
The paper said "cannot be put out on this day", so it was the wrong day.
1-64: "Showed me the garbage chart you can get at city hall."
1-65: What is the writer's main point?
not said it is too hard
he sometimes teaches, but it is not the main point
The last sentence: keeping local rules is important for people who live there.
1-66: Why did the writer get tired of convenience-store bento?
money is an extra point, not the reason
"Because it tasted much the same every day, I gradually got tired of it."
1-67: It refers to the sentence just before: making miso soup was easier than expected and tasty.
1-68: How has the writer changed since starting to cook?
Last sentence: checking vegetable prices became a pleasure. Cooking is 4 days a week, not every day.
1-69: Why did the writer feel sad at first?
An elderly man said, "Forget it, call a Japanese clerk."
1-70: the opposite of what was said
"You don't have to memorise it all. One thing a day is fine."
1-71: Why did the writer think "I'm glad I didn't give up"?
The same man who once asked for a Japanese clerk praised the writer's Japanese.
1-72: What does the writer plan to do next?
Last sentence: "This time I will show her my own notes."
1-73: How much do the two pay?
Adult 500 + child free + swimming class 800 = 1,300 yen.
1-74: How do you join the swimming class?
The class is on Saturday and you must phone by the day before, so by Friday.
1-75: What must the man do first?
The manager wants one more graph, so he says "I'll make the graph first."
1-76: What will the female student bring tomorrow?
She says "I'll just bring a raincoat."
1-77: What will the man do first?
"First, please fill in this form. After writing, take your temperature."
1-78: What will the students cut first?
"Let's start with the carrots and potatoes."
1-79: How will the man get to the airport?
1-80: By what time must the woman submit the papers?
Accounting leaves at 5 and needs 30 min to check: by 4:30.
1-81: he can put up with it
"My company is moving to another town; it would take 1.5 hours."
1-82: What did the woman say was good about the film?
1-83: What will the man talk about in the speech contest?
"I decided to talk about memories of an old lady in my neighbourhood."
1-84: Why doesn't the woman buy the bag?
"My computer doesn't fit, and I need it for work."
1-85: What did the man do at the weekend?
"I went to help my brother move."
1-86: What does the man say is most important for good sleep?
"The most important is getting up at the same time every morning."
1-87: What is the woman talking about?
After plastic bags started costing money, far fewer people use them.
1-88: What is the teacher talking about?
The library will open until 9 p.m. and close on Saturdays.
1-89: What does the man think of the restaurant?
"Tasty, but pricey, and I waited 40 minutes."
1-90: What do you say entering the teacher's room?
When entering a room: 失礼します.
1-91: What do you say to pay at a restaurant?
Asking for the bill: お会計をお願いします.
1-92: A coworker looks pale. What do you say?
Showing concern: 大丈夫ですか.
1-93: You can't reach the luggage rack. What do you say to the person next to you?
Asking for help: 〜ていただけませんか.
1-94: "Can you do this document by tomorrow?"
Accepting a request: はい、わかりました.
1-95: Reply: いえいえ、また行きましょう.
1-97: Giving a reason: ちょっと用事があって.
1-98: "Do you mind if I open the window?"
Permission: ええ、かまいませんよ.
1-99: "Do you think you can come to next week's party?"
1-101: 私も今来たところです.
1-102: "Teacher, there's something I'd like to ask."
